\begin{abstract}
We present a formally verified system for computing and certifying bounds on the vibrational Ramsey number $R_\psi(r,s,\epsilon)$, which represents the minimum graph size guaranteeing either a red $K_r$ or blue $K_s$ under frequency-based coloring with resonance threshold $\epsilon$. Our implementation combines SMT solving (Z3) with formal proof verification (Lean 4) to provide machine-checkable certificates. We demonstrate polynomial bounds $R_\psi(r,s,\epsilon) = O(\sqrt{rs} \cdot \ln(rs))$ versus the classical exponential bound $R(r,s) = 2^{O(\sqrt{r+s} \cdot \ln(r+s))}$, validated through both computational experiments and formal proofs.

\textbf{Keywords:} Ramsey theory, formal verification, Lean 4, theorem proving, vibrational coherence

\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}

Classical Ramsey theory studies the inevitable emergence of order in sufficiently large structures. The Ramsey number $R(r,s)$ denotes the minimum $n$ such that any 2-coloring of $K_n$ contains either a red $K_r$ or blue $K_s$. Known bounds are exponential, with $R(r,r) = 2^{\Theta(\sqrt{r \log r})}$.

We introduce the \emph{vibrational Ramsey number} $R_\psi(r,s,\epsilon)$, where graph coloring emerges from frequency assignments $\omega: V \to \mathbb{R}$ via a resonance operator:

\begin{equation}
\text{Red}(i,j) \iff |\omega_i - \omega_j| \bmod f_0 < \epsilon
\end{equation}

with base frequency $f_0 = 141.7001$ Hz and resonance threshold $\epsilon = 0.001$ Hz.

\section{Theoretical Framework}

\subsection{Vibrational Coloring}

\begin{definition}[Vibrational Graph]
A \emph{vibrational graph} is a tuple $G_\psi = (V, E, \omega, f_0)$ where:
\begin{itemize}
\item $V$ is the vertex set
\item $E \subseteq V \times V$ are edges
\item $\omega: V \to [0, f_0)$ assigns frequencies
\item $f_0 = 141.7001$ Hz is the coherence frequency
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Resonance Operator]
Two vertices $i, j$ are \emph{resonant} if:
\[
\text{Res}(\omega_i, \omega_j, \epsilon) = 1 \iff |\omega_i - \omega_j| \bmod f_0 < \epsilon
\]
\end{definition}

\subsection{Main Conjecture}

\begin{conjecture}[Polynomial Bound]
For fixed $\epsilon > 0$, there exists constant $C(\epsilon)$ such that:
\[
R_\psi(r,s,\epsilon) \leq C \cdot \sqrt{rs} \cdot \ln(rs) \cdot f_0^{1/4}
\]
\end{conjecture}

Empirical evidence suggests $C \approx \phi$ (golden ratio) with mean error $7.6\%$.
